story.title: Beauty and the Beast
story.description: A young woman offers to live in a cursed beast's castle in her father's place, and learns to look past appearances.
story.author: Gabrielle-Suzanne de Villeneuve & Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont

chapters.name: A Promise of Return
chapters.summary: A ruined merchant takes one rose he was not offered, and the debt he incurs is paid by the daughter who asked for it.

chapters.name: The Same Question Every Night
chapters.summary: Beauty is given everything in the castle except the one thing she asks for, and refuses the one thing she is asked, every night, for as long as she stays.

chapters.name: Ten Days, and One Late
chapters.summary: Her sisters keep her past the term on purpose. What she does with the mirror decides which of two endings the Fairy allows.

scenes.name: One rose, and nothing else
scenes.summary: The merchant, leaving on the rumour of a recovered ship, asks his three daughters what they want brought back. Two ask for gowns and jewels. Beauty asks for a rose, thinking she is asking for nothing.

scenes.name: Lost in the forest
scenes.summary: The ship is gone and so is the last of the money. Snow closes the road home, and the merchant follows a light through the trees to a castle where the doors open, the fire is lit, and there is not a soul to thank.

scenes.name: The stolen rose and the terms
scenes.summary: Leaving at dawn, he cuts one rose from the garden for Beauty, and the Beast is there before the stem is down. The terms are his life, or a daughter who comes in his place and comes willingly.

scenes.name: Beauty takes his place
scenes.summary: Beauty hears the whole of it and goes, over her father's refusal, because the promise names her and she will not have it paid by anyone else. The Beast meets her at the door and asks whether she came of her own will.

scenes.name: Dinner at the long table
scenes.summary: She dines alone and the Beast sits at the far end and talks to her, badly. Everything she says she would like appears before she has finished saying it, which makes the one thing she cannot have very conspicuous.

scenes.name: The library he opens for her
scenes.summary: The Beast gives her a library she could not read through in a lifetime, and does not follow her into it. It is the first thing he offers that she wanted before he offered it.

scenes.name: The same question every night
scenes.summary: Every night at the end of dinner he asks her to marry him, and every night she says no, and every night he accepts it and wishes her goodnight. Neither of them ever pretends the question is not going to be asked again.

scenes.name: Leave to depart
scenes.summary: She asks to see her father, and the Beast gives her a ring that carries her home and back, and a mirror that shows her anything she wishes to see. He asks only that she return in ten days, and warns her plainly that he will not survive her not doing so.

scenes.name: Her sisters' envy
scenes.summary: Her sisters find her well dressed, well fed and well treated, and cannot bear it. They weep and cling and beg her to stay one more day, and then another, and count them carefully.

scenes.name: A vision in the mirror
scenes.summary: On the eleventh day Beauty looks into the mirror and sees the Beast lying by the fountain in his garden, not moving. She turns the ring that same moment, without finishing the sentence she was speaking.

scenes.name: A merciful ending
scenes.summary: Beauty says she loves him and the curse breaks. Out of kindness she asks the Fairy to spare her sisters, and the Fairy grants it - and says, to the room, that a mercy nobody earned is still a mercy given.

scenes.name: A just ending
scenes.summary: Beauty says she loves him and the curse breaks. The Fairy judges the sisters by what they did, and leaves them as statues at the castle gate to watch a happiness they tried to prevent, until they can admit their own part in it.

characters.name: Beauty
characters.description: A merchant's youngest daughter, an avid reader with a generous nature, who asks for the smallest thing anyone asks for and pays the largest price for it. She goes to the castle because the promise has her name in it.
characters.personality: Gentle, thoughtful, and unfailingly kind, even to those who mistreat her.
characters.motivation: Wants to spare her father's life, and later, to be honest with her own heart about the Beast.
characters.qualities: Loyal, generous, and able to see past appearances to what someone truly is.
characters.weaknesses: So devoted to others that she nearly lets the Beast die of grief rather than admit her own feelings sooner.
characters.biography: The merchant's youngest daughter, unlike her vain sisters in temperament, who offers her own freedom to save her father from the Beast's wrath.
characters.plannedTimeline: Returns to the castle in time, confesses her love, and breaks the curse - marrying the prince the Beast once was.

characters.name: The Beast
characters.title: Cursed prince
characters.description: A prince turned into a beast by a fairy, who may only be freed by being loved of his own free will - which is why he asks the same question every night and accepts the same answer every night.
characters.personality: Fearsome in appearance but courteous and melancholy underneath, aware of how frightening he seems.
characters.motivation: Hopes, without much confidence, that Beauty could one day love him despite his form.
characters.qualities: Patient, generous, and consistently gentle with Beauty despite his monstrous looks.
characters.weaknesses: So convinced of his own unlovability that he nearly wastes away from grief when Beauty stays away.
characters.biography: A prince who, as a spoiled and unkind boy, refused shelter to a fairy in disguise and was cursed to wear a beast's form until he is loved for who he truly is.
characters.plannedTimeline: Nearly dies of grief waiting for Beauty's return, then is restored to his human form once she confesses her love.

characters.name: The Merchant
characters.title: Beauty's father
characters.description: A merchant who lost his fortune at sea and his way in the forest on the same journey. He takes one rose without asking and spends the rest of the story trying to keep his daughter from paying for it.
characters.personality: Loving and honorable, quick to blame himself for the danger he brings on his daughter.
characters.motivation: Wants only to provide for his children and keep his word, even at the cost of his own life.
characters.qualities: Devoted and honest, willing to return to the Beast's castle to face his punishment himself.
characters.weaknesses: His once-great fortune, lost when his trading ships were feared sunk at sea, left the family unable to protect themselves from misfortune.
characters.biography: A once-wealthy merchant whose ships were lost at sea, reduced to a modest country life until a detour through an enchanted forest changes his family's fate again.
characters.plannedTimeline: Is spared by the Beast and reunited with Beauty after the curse breaks.

characters.name: The Elder Sister
characters.description: Beauty's sister, who cannot forgive her for being content with less. She is the one who counts the days aloud and pretends she is not counting.
characters.personality: Proud and self-absorbed, quick to resent Beauty's good fortune.
characters.motivation: Hopes Beauty's return to the castle will end badly for her, out of sheer jealousy.
characters.qualities: Sharp-witted enough to talk Beauty into staying past her promised week.
characters.weaknesses: Her envy blinds her to how her scheming nearly costs the Beast his life.
characters.biography: One of Beauty's two older sisters, who never forgave the family's fall from wealth and resents that Beauty seems happier for it.
characters.plannedTimeline: Left humbled once the curse breaks and Beauty's fortune is restored, her fate softened only by Beauty's mercy.

characters.name: The Second Sister
characters.description: The other sister, just as proud and just as envious, and readier to say out loud what the elder only arranges.
characters.personality: Vain and easily wounded by pride, quick to follow her elder sister's lead.
characters.motivation: Shares her sister's hope that delaying Beauty will cause her misfortune.
characters.qualities: Charming enough in company to mask her jealousy from outsiders.
characters.weaknesses: Cares more about appearances and status than about her sister's happiness.
characters.biography: The second of Beauty's older sisters, just as unwilling as the eldest to accept the family's more modest life.
characters.plannedTimeline: Shares in her sister's humbled fate once the curse breaks, spared only through Beauty's kindness.

characters.name: The Fairy
characters.description: The fairy who laid the curse and has watched in silence ever since to see whether it works. She appears once, at the end, and what she does then depends entirely on what Beauty asks her for.
characters.personality: Just but unforgiving of cruelty, testing character before granting mercy.
characters.motivation: Wants the prince to learn true kindness before allowing the curse to be lifted.
characters.qualities: Powerful and patient, willing to wait years to see whether her lesson takes hold.
characters.weaknesses: Her judgment can be severe - she is prepared to punish Beauty's sisters as harshly as she once punished the prince.
characters.biography: A fairy who, disguised as a beggar, was refused shelter by a spoiled young prince and cursed him into a beast until he could learn to love and be loved for who he truly is.
characters.plannedTimeline: Reveals herself once the curse breaks, and decides the sisters' fate depending on the version of the ending.

locations.name: The Forest
locations.description: The wood between the port road and the castle, where the snow closes in and the only light for a day in any direction is one that should not be there.
locations.climate: Rural and plain, a world away from the city life the family once knew.
locations.culture: A humbled household where hard work has replaced the comforts of wealth.
locations.politics: No authority beyond the Merchant's own quiet leadership of his household.

locations.name: The Beast's Castle
locations.description: An enchanted castle where every wish is granted before it is finished being spoken, and where the two things Beauty wants - to see her father, and to see the Beast as he was - are the only two it cannot supply.
locations.climate: Grand and warm indoors, tended by unseen enchanted servants.
locations.culture: A solitary court of one, where every comfort is offered and every meal shared only with the Beast.
locations.politics: Ruled entirely by the Beast, though the enchantment itself answers to no one but the Fairy.

locations.name: The Enchanted Garden
locations.description: The rose garden and the fountain, where the Beast goes when he wants to be alone and where everything in this story that matters is either taken, given, or nearly lost.
locations.climate: Lush and blooming year-round, tended by the same unseen magic as the castle.
locations.culture: A quiet retreat, the one place the Beast allows himself to be seen at his most vulnerable.

locations.name: The Road Home
locations.description: The road the merchant could not travel in the snow, and that the ring makes unnecessary. It is still there, and it is still ten days long, which is the whole point of the term.

locations.name: The Merchant's House
locations.description: The modest house the family moved to when the ships were lost, where two daughters have never stopped resenting the move and the third has never mentioned it.

worldRules.title: A Promise of Return
worldRules.description: The Beast can only be freed by being loved of his own free will, which makes force useless to him. When he lets Beauty go he is not being generous - a Beauty who could not leave could not choose to stay, and a stay that is not chosen is worth nothing against the curse.

worldRules.title: The Beast's Enchanted Gifts
worldRules.description: A ring that carries its wearer between the two houses instantly, and a mirror that shows any place or person. Between them they remove every practical reason Beauty could have for being late, so that being late can only ever be a choice.

worldRules.title: Nothing Is Taken Without Consent
worldRules.description: The Beast asks his question every night and accepts the answer every night. He does not hold Beauty by force; he holds her by a promise her father made and she chose to keep - which is a different thing, and the whole point of the curse.

notes.title: Continuity: the term is ten days
notes.body: The ring makes the journey instant, so the ten days are never about travel. Every scene at her father's house has to make clear that she could be back in a heartbeat and is not going.

notes.title: Visual motif: given before it is asked for
notes.body: The castle answers wishes before they are finished. Use it to make the two things it cannot give - her father, and his old face - land harder every time.

notes.title: Revision goal: the endings differ in one word
notes.body: Both endings break the curse. What splits them is whether Beauty asks the Fairy for mercy or leaves her to judge. Keep everything before the split identical so the difference is entirely hers.

items.name: The Enchanted Rose
items.description: The only gift Beauty asked her father to bring her, and the only thing in the garden the Beast had not already decided to give away. Everything in the story follows from one stem being cut without asking.

items.name: The Magic Ring
items.description: A ring that carries whoever turns it between the castle and the house at once. It removes every obstacle to Beauty leaving, which is exactly what makes her staying away a decision.

items.name: The Magic Mirror
items.description: A mirror that shows whoever holds it any place or person they wish to see. The Beast gives Beauty the means to check on him at any moment, and never once asks her to use it.
